- The page also refers generally to “Artifacts from the Antikythera Wreck,” “objects,” and “the entire collection of artifacts,” but does not name any additional physical artifacts or finds.
- No materials, discovery campaigns or years, museum inventory/catalog numbers, or image descriptions are stated for the other references.

## Artifacts and finds

| Object or find | Material | Discovery campaign/year | Details stated on the page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arm of a statue | Bronze | 1900–01 | Retrieved by Captain Dimitrios Kondos shortly after diver Elias Stadiatis reported the wreck. |
| “The Philosopher” | Bronze | 1900–01 | One of the bronze statues recovered by the middle of 1901. |
| Youth of Antikythera (Ephebe) | Bronze | 1900–01 | Dated to c. 340 BC. |
| Hercules statue | Marble | 1900–01 | One of the thirty-six marble sculptures recovered. |
| Odysseus statue | Marble | 1900–01 | One of the thirty-six marble sculptures recovered. |
| Diomedes statue | Marble | 1900–01 | One of the thirty-six marble sculptures recovered. |
| Hermes statue | Marble | 1900–01 | One of the thirty-six marble sculptures recovered. |
| Apollo statue | Marble | 1900–01 | One of the thirty-six marble sculptures recovered. |
| Three horse statues | Marble | 1900–01 | Three marble statues of horses were recovered. |
| Fourth horse statue | Marble | 1900–01 | Dropped during recovery and lost on the sea floor. |
| Bronze lyre | Bronze | 1900–01 | Recovered by the sponge divers. |
| Pieces of glasswork | Glass | 1900–01 | Recovered by the sponge divers. |
| Lead scupper pipes | Lead | 1900–01 | Recovered ship’s equipment. |
| Hull sheeting | Material not explicitly stated in the 1900–01 recovery description | 1900–01 | Recovered ship’s equipment. |
| Sounding leads | Lead | 1900–01 | A set weighed 6 and 14 kg (13 and 31 lb). The page states that these are the only sounding weights ever discovered on an ancient shipwreck in the Aegean. |
| Small and common artifacts | Materials not specified | 1900–01 | Many other small and common artifacts were found; the entire assemblage was taken to the National Archaeological Museum in Athens. |
| Antikythera mechanism | Severely corroded bronze | 17 May 1902 | A gear wheel was embedded in the object, with legible inscriptions in Greek. Valerios Stais discovered it while studying the artifacts at the National Archaeological Museum. It was originally thought to be an early mechanised clock or an astrolabe and is sometimes called the world’s oldest known analog computer. |
| Domestic utensils | Materials not specified | Other; associated with dating evidence | The page states that domestic utensils and objects from the ship were similar to those known from other first-century BC contexts. |
| Other objects from the ship | Materials not specified | Other; associated with dating evidence | Mentioned together with domestic utensils as evidence supporting an early first-century BC date. |
| Amphorae | Material not specified | Other; recovered before the dating assessment | The amphorae recovered from the wreck indicated a date of 80–70 BC. |
| Hellenistic pottery | Pottery | Other; recovered before the dating assessment | Indicated a date of 75–50 BC. |
| Roman ceramics | Ceramic | Other; recovered before the dating assessment | Similar to known mid-first-century types. |
| Coins | Material not explicitly stated | 1970s | Recovered during Jacques Cousteau’s work with associates; they were minted between 76 and 67 BC. |
| Four hull planks | Elm wood | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. The page states that remains of hull planks showed the ship was made of elm. |
| Ceramic jars | Ceramic | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. |
| Bronze coins | Bronze | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team; the coins helped date the wreck more accurately. |
| Silver coins | Silver | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team; the coins helped date the wreck more accurately. |
| Pieces of bronze sculptures | Bronze | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. |
| Pieces of marble sculptures | Marble | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. |
| Bronze statuettes | Bronze | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. |
| Gold jewelry | Gold | 1976 | Several pieces were recovered. |
| Human remains of crew and passengers | Human skeletal material | 1976 | Recovered by Jacques Cousteau’s team. |
| Head of a marble statue | Marble | 2021 survey program | Possibly the missing head of a statue of Hercules recovered from the same site in 1902. |
| Wood elements from the hull or decks | Wood | 2014–2016 | Recovered during subsequent excavations by the Hellenic Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities. |
| Components of two anchors | Lead | 2014–2016 | Recovered during the excavations. |
| Enormous salvage ring | Lead | 2014–2016 | Recovered during the excavations. |
| Hull sheeting | Lead | 2014–2016 | Recovered during the excavations. |
| Nails and spikes | Bronze | 2014–2016 | Several bronze nails and spikes were recovered. |
| Rigging ring | Bronze | 2014–2016 | Recovered during the excavations. |
| Two large spears from statues | Bronze | 2014–2016 | Recovered among the luxury goods. |
| Left hand of a statue | Marble | 2014–2016 | Recovered among the luxury goods. |
| Ornate glass bowls | Glass | 2014–2016 | Recovered among the luxury goods. |
| Intact ceramic jars | Ceramic | 2014–2016 | Several intact jars of different styles were recovered. |
| Gold ring | Gold | 2014–2016 | Very similar to one recovered in 1976. |
| Dolphin, or war dolphin | Lead with an iron spike | 2014–2016 | A 100-kilogram (220 lb) lead bulb tipped with an iron spike. It was intended to be dropped from the ship’s yardarm through the deck and hull of an attacking vessel. The page states that this is the only example of a war dolphin ever discovered. |
| Human skeleton nicknamed *Pamphilos* | Human skeletal material | 31 August 2016 | A 2000-year-old human skeleton discovered at the shipwreck. |
| Bronze arm from a sculpture | Bronze | September–October 2017 | Recovered during the Hellenic Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities excavation. |
| Other fragments of bronze statues | Bronze | September–October 2017 and October 2019 | Recovered with the bronze arm. |

| Heracles of Antikythera statue/body | Marble | Other: 1901. The body was brought to light by divers who discovered the wreck of Antikythera. | `No 5742` | “The statue in the NAMA” |
| Left hand of the Heracles of Antikythera | Not separately stated; the sculpture’s listed medium is marble | Other: 2016 | No separate number stated | No separate image description stated |
| (Presumed) head of the Heracles of Antikythera | Not separately stated; the sculpture’s listed medium is marble | Other: 2022 | No separate number stated | No separate image description stated |

- The body is 2.50 m tall.
- The unattached head is 65 cm.
- The sculpture is eroded, with fragments missing.
- The statue is housed in the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.
